data.text: The somatosensory system handles touch, proprioception, and kinesthesis through at least nine major types of receptors. Proprioception is the conscious awareness of body part pose and movement, while kinesthesis provides information on movement parameters like velocity and force. These receptors transform inputs into neural impulses that the brain processes into perception and can send back to cause corrective motor actions.
points: The somatosensory system handles touch, proprioception, and kinesthesis.
Proprioception is the awareness of body part pose, while kinesthesis is the awareness of movement parameters like velocity and force.
At least nine major types of receptors in the skin and muscles detect touch, proprioception, and kinesthesis.
Receptors transform inputs into neural impulses that the brain processes into perception and can send back to cause corrective motor actions.

data.text: Haptic perception is the perception of an object's geometric shape through touch, while haptic exploration involves manipulating objects to infer that shape. Different types of haptic exploration are used to create a geometric mental model of an object's properties. By allowing users to feel the virtual environment, haptic perception and exploration increase the immersive experience.
points: Haptic perception is the perception of an object's geometric shape through touch.
Haptic exploration involves manipulating objects to infer their shape.
Different types of haptic exploration are used to create a geometric mental model of an object's properties.
Incorporating haptic perception and exploration increases immersion by allowing users to feel the virtual environment.

data.text: Touch sensation in XR can be provided by engineered force feedback devices, although precisely controlling haptic pin arrays to simulate surface textures is challenging. Real-world objects are sometimes called tangible user interfaces and are used as avatars to provide touch feedback, which is generally considered less challenging than creating computer-controlled haptic devices. These tangible user interfaces work by aligning the real and virtual worlds.
points: Touch sensation in XR can be provided by engineered force feedback devices.
Haptic pin arrays can simulate surface textures, but controlling them precisely enough is challenging.
Real-world objects are sometimes called tangible user interfaces and are used as avatars to provide touch feedback.
Using real objects for touch is generally considered less challenging than creating computer-controlled haptic devices.
Tangible user interfaces work by aligning the real and virtual worlds.

data.text: Taste and smell are generally grouped as chemical senses that have much less research and fewer devices than vision, audio, and touch. Olfactory displays usually use pumps to provide smells that are relatively easier to deliver for personal experiences than on a room scale and may help reduce cybersickness to some extent. Taste interfaces use electrodes but are generally quite difficult to develop without people eating food.
points: Taste and smell are generally grouped as chemical senses that respond to chemical stimuli.
There is much less research and fewer devices for these senses than for vision, audio, and touch.
Olfactory displays usually use pumps to provide smells, which are relatively easier to deliver for personal experiences than on a room scale.
Smells can induce strong cognitive and emotional responses and may help reduce cybersickness to some extent.
Taste interfaces use electrodes to simulate tastes but are generally quite difficult to develop without people eating food.

data.text: The human somatosensory system includes receptors for touch, proprioception, and kinesthesis. Research prototypes for taste and smell are not very popular or commonly used in commercial VR systems. Chapter 13 of Virtual Reality by LaValle can be used to obtain more details on these topics.
